column1: # G13 after B2: how much negative scaling is the ENGINE's?
# Host: c6id.8xlarge, 32 vCPU, Debian 12 (6.1.0), XFS on instance NVMe,
# THP off, numa_balancing off. libdb at c0f541e6f (U6b fix live:
# HAVE_MUTEX_HYBRID=1, so mut_tas.c is compiled in for the first time).
# btree, -d nosync, 20s measured, 10s warmup. Arms AND thread counts
# alternated within each rep.
# ARM A/B: one binary per arm, differing ONLY at the six DB_RMW call sites.
rep
# medians, t=8 -> t=32:
#   after   564810 -> 524439  =  -7.1%   (retry/commit 0.031, 184x fewer)
# So the -76.8% originally attributed to the engine was substantially the
# driver's missing DB_RMW. cv: before t=8 20.0%, after t=8 0.4%.
# --- THE GATE, same binary, reps=9, ONLY the warehouse count differs -------
# scale
# The gate defaults to SCALE=96; my A/B used 32, which is why they disagree.
# Both are correct measurements of different working-set sizes.
# COUNTER-INTUITIVE AND LOAD-BEARING: scale 96 has MORE warehouses, hence LESS
# per-row contention, yet scales WORSE. So the residual decline is not row
# conflict. It is also not I/O: the scale-96 record set is 0.23 GiB against a
# cache over 1 GB, and db_stat reports "Threads waited on page I/O: 0".
# The subsystem table below is WRONG and is kept only so the error is visible.
# I collected it with `db_stat -l`, believing -l meant "lock". IT MEANS LOG.
# So "lock_region_waits 774650 -> 641738" is the LOG region latch, and the
# conclusion "the residual is the lock region latch" does not follow from it.
# The lock subsystem is `db_stat -c`. Re-measured correctly on a 64 vCPU
# c6id.16xlarge at scale 96, stats CLEARED before each run, per-commit:
#   t   commits   part/cmt  lockeralloc/cmt  region/cmt  objq/cmt  conflict/cmt
# per-commit growth t=8 -> t=64:
#   locker-alloc  5.2x   <-- fastest-growing LATCH wait, 15% of acquisitions
#   lock-conflict 4.6x       (a consequence, not a latch)
#   partition     1.9x
#   region        1.3x
#   obj-queue    18.8x       but absolute value is negligible (0.009/commit)
# THE SERIALIZATION POINT IS mtx_locker_stripe[0]. Despite living in the
# stripe array it is NOT a stripe: lock.h:383 documents it as the LOCKER
# ALLOCATION latch, guarding region-wide state with no per-bucket home (the
# free_lockers list, the ulinks list, nlockers, and the lock_id/cur_maxid
# counters). It is taken ~4x per transaction, by __lock_id,
# __lock_getlocker (txn_begin, txn.c:588) and __lock_freelocker (txn end).
# __lock_getlocker holds it across the WHOLE call -- including the common case
# where the free list is non-empty and only a bucket is touched -- purely to
# make the free-list emptiness test atomic with the refill.
# --- SUPERSEDED (collected with the wrong db_stat flag) --------------------
# subsystem
mpool_bucket_waits
mpool_region_waits
page_io_waits
lock_region_waits
